gcd_lemma.d1: gcd(U,V) divides 2 because any odd p dividing 2TS and T^2-S^2 would divide both T and S.
gcd_lemma.d2: gcd(U,V) divides 2: if odd p divides both, U-V=2*S*(2*T-S); p|S forces p|T, while 2T=S mod p substituted into U forces p|T; both contradict primitiveness.
gcd_lemma.consequence: No odd prime divides U and V simultaneously.

odd_prime_pattern_lemma.support: If U*V*A*B is a rational square, every odd prime appearing in the squareclass of any factor divides a*b*(a^2-b^2).
odd_prime_pattern_lemma.reason: An odd squareclass prime must occur to odd valuation in at least two factors. Pairwise common divisibility is controlled by gcd(U,V)=1 at odd p and the linear identities A=aU+bV, B=bU+aV.
odd_prime_pattern_lemma.categories_are_disjoint: For gcd(a,b)=1, an odd prime cannot divide two of a, b, a^2-b^2.
